description: Two-panel composite figure of generic property plots. (a) Density (y-axis, g/cm3, labelled 6-8 with major ticks every 0.5) versus Alloy content (x-axis, wt%, labelled 0-16 with major ticks every 2) carrying five labelled lines: Cr, Mn, Si, Al and C. All lines start just below the 8.0 g/cm3 gridline at 0 wt%. The C line is drawn steeply downward and stops at ~2 wt%, just above the 7.0 gridline; the blue Al line falls furthest, ending just above the 6.0 gridline at 16 wt%; the ordering of density reduction at 16 wt% is Al > Si (ends near the 7.0 gridline) > Mn (ends between 7.5 and 8.0) > Cr (ends just below 7.8). (b) Young's modulus (y-axis, GPa, labelled 100-220, major ticks every 20) versus Al content (x-axis, wt%, 0-16). Four literature datasets are overlaid: Frommeyer [24] (red line, open diamond markers, spanning roughly 6-9 wt% Al), Kubo [28] (dotted), Yamamoto-Taniguchi [28] (dashed) and Fukuroi-Shibuya [28] (solid blue). All curves begin near the 220 GPa gridline at 0 wt% Al and decrease with Al content; the solid blue curve falls to a minimum near the 140 GPa gridline at ~12-13 wt%, then rises back to about 158 GPa at 16 wt%. Together the panels show Al is the strongest density-reducing addition yet simultaneously lowers Young's modulus. No scale bars; neither panel prints numeric data labels.
measured_quantities: density reduction per wt% alloy addition (g/cm3 per wt%)
change of Young's modulus per wt% Al (%)

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots Density (g/cm3, axis 6-8) against Alloy content (wt%, axis 0-16) and contains five curves labelled Cr, Mn, Si, Al and C.
In panel (a) all five curves start just below the 8.0 g/cm3 gridline at 0 wt% alloy content, i.e. from the same ferritic-iron baseline.
In panel (a) the C curve is the steepest and stops at about 2 wt%, whereas the Al curve extends to 16 wt% and ends just above the 6.0 g/cm3 gridline.
At 16 wt% alloy content the density reduction in panel (a) is ordered Al > Si > Mn > Cr, with Si ending near the 7.0 gridline, Mn between 7.5 and 8.0, and Cr just below 7.8.
Panel (b) plots Young's modulus (GPa, axis 100-220) against Al content (wt%, axis 0-16) with four overlaid datasets: Frommeyer [24], Kubo [28], Yamamoto-Taniguchi [28] and Fukuroi-Shibuya [28].

In panel (b) all curves start near the 220 GPa gridline at 0 wt% Al and decrease monotonically up to about 12 wt% Al, with the solid blue Fukuroi-Shibuya curve passing through a minimum near the 140 GPa gridline at ~12-13 wt% and then rising again to roughly 158 GPa at 16 wt%.
The Frommeyer [24] data in panel (b) are plotted as a red line with open diamond markers confined to roughly the 6-9 wt% Al range, whereas the three [28] datasets cover the full 0-16 wt% Al range.

The caption states that (a) shows the density reduction of ferritic iron by elements lighter than Fe, and (b) the reduction of Young's modulus of Fe-Al steels in the annealed state as a function of Al content.

The citing text states that the density of steel decreases linearly with increasing addition of the elements Al, C, Si and Mn, and that the data for Al came from literature [24] while other elements were calculated from formulae derived by Bohnenkamp and Sandström [27].
The citing text states that Al has emerged as the chief alloying element in low-density bulk steels and that Si is sometimes added in combination with Al.

The citing text states that the Young's modulus data in panel (b) were measured with dynamic methods (resonance or ultrasonic) which are more precise than quasi-static tensile tests, and that a 2-2.5% reduction in Young's modulus per 1% Al addition is obtained.

The citing text attributes the decrease of Young's modulus with increasing Al to a reduction of lattice energy of the Fe-Al solid solution and a larger distance between coexisting Fe and Al atoms, and adds that Si and Cr slightly increase the E modulus while Mn slightly decreases it in steels with high Al.

subfigures.description: Line plot of Density (g/cm3, axis 6-8) versus Alloy content (wt%, axis 0-16) with five labelled curves Cr, Mn, Si, Al and C, all originating just below 8.0 g/cm3 at 0 wt%. C terminates at ~2 wt%, Al (blue) decreases most strongly to ~6.1 g/cm3 at 16 wt%, followed by Si, Mn and Cr in descending effect.

Line plot of Young's modulus (GPa, axis 100-220) versus Al content (wt%, axis 0-16) with four overlaid literature datasets: Frommeyer [24] (red line with open diamond markers), Kubo [28] (dotted), Yamamoto-Taniguchi [28] (dashed) and Fukuroi-Shibuya [28] (solid blue). All curves start near 210-215 GPa at 0 wt% Al and decrease; the solid blue curve reaches a minimum near 140 GPa at ~12-13 wt% then recovers slightly towards 158 GPa at 16 wt%.
